subject: Private deployment node variance / performance sync with CPO - Sunspire
messages:
From: Sunspire Support <support@sunspirehealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 07:45:00 +0000
Subject: Sudden p95 / 503 spike on our Frankfurt private cluster

Hi Mina,

We're seeing a sharp degradation on our Frankfurt private deployment (cluster: sunspire-fr1) that started around 03/28 02:30 UTC. Symptoms: p95 generation latency rose from ~1.5s to ~6.2s, sustained 503 error rate ~6-8% over the last 45 minutes, and overall throughput dropped ~28%. The problem appears node-localized: telemetry shows Node-3 having higher CPU and sustained mutex contention.

We've attached a perf snapshot and a short heap dump (perf_snapshot_20280328.json, heap_profile_node3.png). No config changes on our side this morning. This is impacting a live triage flow for our clinicians — they are seeing timeouts and failing requests.

Can your team confirm whether this looks like a runtime/kernel regression or if we should scale capacity? We can schedule a quick joint debugging call if helpful.

Thanks,
Priya Khan
Director, Platform Operations
Sunspire Health

Attachments: perf_snapshot_20280328.json, heap_profile_node3.png

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Khan <priya.khan@sunspirehealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 08:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 / 503 spike on our Frankfurt private cluster

Hi Priya — thanks for the quick heads up and attachments.

Irene and Laura, looping you in to triage immediately. Please validate whether this is a single-node kernel/GC regression or a workload pattern (prefix-hotshard) causing KV cache thrashing. If we confirm node-localized resource pressure, propose these near-term actions we can take while we debug:

- Start a temporary 25% capacity boost (add 2 additional inference nodes) to buy breathing room
- Pin traffic away from Node-3 (route offloading) and enable conservative batching on the affected pool
- Collect a full kernel profile and KV cache traces; share to the incident Drive folder and JIRA ticket INF-4721

Priya — would you be available for a 30m call at 09:00 UTC to review a proposed mitigation?

I'll escalate to Markus for an executive decision on any capacity or SLA exceptions.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com
+1 415 555 0128

Attachments: none

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Khan <priya.khan@sunspirehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 08:44:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 / 503 spike on our Frankfurt private cluster

Quick initial findings from the first 25 minutes of triage (INF-4721):

- Node-3 shows repeated KV cache evictions correlated with a small set of long-running prefix-heavy requests — likely a working-set mismatch causing excessive cache churn
- Heap growth on the inference worker process on Node-3 is higher than other nodes; flame graph attached (heap_profile_node3.png). No immediate OOMs, but GC pause time spiked coincident with the p95 bump
- Kernel-level syscall latency for cudaMemcpy seems elevated on Node-3 vs Node-1/2 (we've pulled perf counters)

Immediate tactical actions taken:
- We drained Node-3 from serving and re-routed 100% of traffic off it (routing rule applied at 08:35 UTC)
- Enabled conservative batching for the Frankfurt pool to reduce KV pressure (08:40 UTC)

Effect: p95 improved from 6.2s -> ~2.1s after traffic was rerouted, and 503s dropped under 1.5%. Throughput is still ~15% below baseline, which suggests warmed cache and node replacement will be needed.

Next steps I'm pushing: full kernel trace (20–30m), reproduction run on canary, and a short runbook for Sunspire to add 2 nodes as a capacity buffer. Copying the incident folder here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1SunspirePerf and we created INF-4721.

- Irene
Irene Choi
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: heap_profile_node3.png

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 09:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 / 503 spike on our Frankfurt private cluster

This needs CPO attention and a short exec sync with Sunspire. Marking high priority.

Decision items for the next 60–90 minutes (we can action without contract changes; we will record any SLA exception for billing review):

1) Approve immediate capacity buffer: add 2 replacement inference nodes to sunspire-fr1 (25% boost). Approved.
2) Require a canary run of the latest runtime kernel roll (patch candidate: runtime-kernel-3.18.4) on a non-production shard to validate syscall/copy fixes. Irene, schedule and runbook please.
3) Authorize a short-lived fallback to the quantized model variant for latency-sensitive routes while we root-cause cache churn. Laura to coordinate with Priya on route tagging.

Mina — please prepare a 1-page exec summary for Priya's CPO and propose a 30-minute sync window with our CPO and Sunspire's CPO today at 11:00 UTC (or earliest available). Include the observed impact, immediate actions taken, and expected next steps (canary, kernel trace, capacity add, rollback plan).

Markus
Markus Klein
Chief Product Officer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Khan <priya.khan@sunspirehealth.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 14:03:00 +0000
Subject: Sunspire private cluster — exec sync and short-term mitigation summary

Hi Priya — following our triage yesterday, here's a concise summary and proposed next steps. Markus (our CPO) will join the call to review the mitigation plan.

Observed impact (timeline):
- 2028-03-28 02:30 UTC: p95 jump from ~1.5s to ~6.2s at sunspire-fr1, 503s ~6–8%
- 02:35–02:45 UTC: Node-3 exhibited elevated heap and syscall latency; KV cache evictions correlated with a small subset of prefix-heavy requests
- 02:40 UTC: Node-3 drained; routing change applied -> p95 recovered to ~2.1s; 503s fell <1.5% but throughput still down ~15%

Actions completed so far:
- Drained Node-3 and re-routed traffic off the problematic node
- Enabled conservative batching on Frankfurt pool
- Opened JIRA INF-4721 and uploaded perf snapshot and heap_profile_node3.png to the incident Drive folder

Immediate approved mitigations (today):
- Capacity buffer: adding 2 inference nodes to sunspire-fr1 (ETA 25–35 minutes once requested)
- Canary run of runtime-kernel-3.18.4 on a non-prod shard to validate elevated cudaMemcpy/syscall behavior
- Short-lived fallback to the quantized model variant for latency-sensitive routes if we see persistent p95 regressions after node replacement

What we need from Sunspire now:
- Confirm permission to add the 2 nodes to your private cluster (no billing change required for the buffer window; we'll record the action for follow-up)
- 30-minute exec sync today at 11:00 UTC (Markus, Irene, Laura, Mina + Sunspire CPO) to align on canary success criteria and rollback triggers

Attachments: runbook_v2.pdf (incident playbook & rollback steps)

If 11:00 UTC doesn't work, give two alternatives and we'll coordinate. We're standing by for permission to add nodes and to run the canary.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: runbook_v2.pdf, heap_profile_node3.png
